Hardcode the policies into prompts and redeploy the app for each edit
Freeze the model for a year and ignore every weekly policy change
Ground answers with retrieval over versioned manuals plus cited passages
explain: Retrieval grounds answers in current documents without retraining. Weekly fine-tuning or frozen prompts either cost too much or go stale.

q: A booking assistant must check inventory APIs, reserve seats, and send confirmations inside one chat. Which design fits?
options: Static FAQ rules with no tool calls and fixed reply templates
Plain prompts with no API access and hope the model guesses bookings
Batch jobs that email yesterday's inventory with no conversation layer
Agents that reason over tools and call inventory and booking APIs
explain: Bedrock Agents combine a foundation model with tool and API calls for multi-step tasks such as checking inventory, reserving seats, and sending confirmations. Static rules, plain prompts, and batch jobs cannot invoke APIs.
source: Adattata da Udemy – practice test MLA-C01

q: A new ranking model must replace a production model with minimal blast radius. Which rollout best matches the safety constraint?
options: Canary stages with metric alarms and automatic rollback on regression
Full cutover at midnight with no alarms and no rollback procedure
Parallel full-capacity fleets with no traffic split and double billing
Silent redeploy with monitoring disabled to reduce operational cost
explain: Canary stages shift a slice of traffic under alarms with rollback ready. Full cutovers and unmonitored deploys maximize blast radius.

q: A KMS-encrypted S3 dataset feeds SageMaker, but training fails though the bucket policy looks open. What is the most likely trap behind the failure?
options: The dataset is too accurate, so the training algorithm rejects the input
The endpoint instance is too fast, so the training job times out early
The execution role lacks KMS decrypt rights even with S3 read access
The model artifact is too small, so the KMS key refuses to encrypt it
explain: S3 read plus KMS decrypt are separate grants. The classic trap grants bucket access but forgets the key policy, causing access-denied at read time.

q: A dashboards-only analysis claims a campaign caused a sales uplift. Which reasoning flaw should the candidate spot?
options: Dashboards with more charts automatically upgrade correlation to proof
Extra tables in the query convert an observed link into a proven cause
Higher dashboard refresh rates create causal evidence from raw trends
Trends show correlation, while causation needs controlled comparison
explain: Queries and charts describe co-movement but cannot isolate cause. Controlled tests or designed comparisons are required for causal claims.
source: Adattata da Udemy – practice test MLA-C01
